COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
CRJA No. 30 of 2022
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Ram Singh Sammal, Amicus Curiae, for
the appellant.
Mr. Siddhartha Bisht, Brief Holder, for the
State of Uttarakhand.
The appellant to the present Criminal Jail
Appeal is being represented by Mr. R.S. Sammal,
the learned Amicus Curiae, appointed by the Court.
The appellant was tried in Sessions Trial No. 89 of
2017, State Vs. Baljinder alias Balwinder, wherein,
the appellant was convicted and sentence for the
offences under Section 307 and 323 of the IPC, by
the Court of 1st Additional District and Sessions,
Judge, Kashipur, District Udham Singh Nagar.
By the time the judgement of conviction was
rendered on 22nd March, 2022, the appellant had
already served almost more than four years of his
sentence, as he remained in jail ever since 2017.
The learned Trial Court, while rendering the
judgement of conviction, has convicted and
sentenced the appellant to undergo four years of
rigorous imprisonment for the offence under
Section 307 IPC and a fine of Rs. 5,000/- was
imposed upon him, and in any event of default to
deposit the fine, he was directed to undergo further
one month of simple imprisonment.
 Similarly, for the offence under Section 323
of the IPC, he was sentenced for 6 months of simple
imprisonment.
It is stated at the Bar, and which would also
be apparent from the records of the Court below,
that the present appellant has already served his
sentence more than the sentence awarded to him by
the judgement of conviction dated 22nd March,
2022.
 In that eventuality, since the appellant has

already undergone and had served the sentence of
five years one month and five days, on the date of
the judgement, i.e. 22nd March, 2022, and since
there was a doubt, which prevailed with the Court,
while passing the judgement of conviction, as to
whether the period of sentence already served will
amount to be covered by the aspect of undergoing
of sentence, that is being overruled. Since the
appellant has already served his sentence, he is
directed to be released forthwith.
 Accordingly, the Criminal Jail Appeal, is not
required to be ventured into on its own merit, as the
appellant has already undergone the sentences
imposed upon him by the learned Trial Court by
the judgement dated 22nd March, 2022. The
Criminal Jail Appeal is disposed of accordingly.
The Registry is directed to supply the copy of
today's order to the Jail authorities forthwith for
necessary compliance.
